# Parley v0.1.71

This unnotarized test beta restyles Parley's chrome without removing any
function: paper around glass. The terminal stays the one dark surface; the
chrome around it becomes quieter and reads the same way everywhere, with one
glyph for a handoff. Nothing changes in saved data or the agent protocol
(still 34).

## One language for the chrome

Grey builds every structure and colour states one fact, never a vendor: the
accent means a selected pane, a handoff in flight or a routing role; orange
means a person is needed; red means failure; green means connection health
or a result waiting to be read. System type throughout, with hierarchy
carried by weight before size; every id, time and count is monospaced with
tabular digits.

The **wire** is new and is the chrome's only arrow: a thin line with an
arrowhead that points at the pane that owes the reply. It joins the two
vendor monograms in pane headers, the Collaboration Dock, Status Center, the
reviewed Ask composer and the command palette's Ask commands. It turns red
only when the handoff failed.

## The main window

- **Pane headers** read the same way on every pane: monogram, name, a Lead
  chip, the routing role, the wire to the pane it is talking to, the state
  chip, then the folder and Git branch in mono on the right (a dirty tree in
  orange). The selected pane is the ring and the heavier name, no longer a
  tinted header.
- **Notices moved into the status bar.** The banners that stacked above the
  terminals are now one line under them: the connection, this workspace's
  in-flight and returned counts, the top notice with its single action, and
  "+N" for the remaining notices in the same priority order as before. The
  notice's detail is always in its tooltip and in the "+N" menu.
- **The Collaboration Dock is a ledger**: an In flight card with both named
  endpoints as focus buttons, a Returned card for each unread result with
  Open in Status (which opens that exact record) and Mark Read, the runtime
  facts, then the recent handoffs with a time column, the wire, the named
  route and a state chip.
- Sidebar section headings share the 9pt monospaced heading; Needs Attention
  and its counts are orange.

## Status Center, Settings and the launch review

- **Status Center** rows carry a time column, the wire and "A to B"; the
  condition header is a dot and a title; agent rows lead with the vendor
  monogram and a state chip.
- **Settings** sections are a sidebar (General, Appearance, Terminal, Voice,
  Notifications) with a section header, matching the palette's
  "<Section> Settings…" commands. Every control still saves as it changes.
- **The launch review** shows the choices on the left (vendor, where it
  runs, profile, approvals, folders) and, on its own paper to the right, the
  exact "What is carried" and "What is not carried" review. That text is
  unchanged.
- The reviewed Ask composer's header is the wire between the two vendors,
  and VoiceOver hears both vendor names.

## Also in this build

Two checks that failed once each on GitHub's hosted runners now wait for the
fact they read instead of reading it after a fixed delay: the toolbar menu's
disabled state after closing, and the transport's recreation of a removed
processing or outbox folder. Neither had ever failed in the local VM.

## Going back to v0.1.70

Nothing in saved data changes. v0.1.70 has the previous chrome.

## Validation and known limits

The release workflow repeats the following before publishing this beta:
- the deterministic checks and the repository scans;
- the app build and the 25-round Ghostty soak;
- packaging, checksums and packaged-launch verification.

Checked before the pull request merged: 623 native checks, 82 script tests,
both scans, the build and the 25-round soak in a Command Line Tools Tart VM;
and the checks on GitHub's Xcode 26.6 runner. Codex reviewed the change
independently through a Parley delegation (six P2 and one P3 findings, all
applied: real zero-size layout fallbacks, the dock card's names on their own
row, Open in Status revealing the record, the composer's VoiceOver label, a
workspace-scoped in-flight count, Returned from the authoritative unread
records, named routes on recent rows). The screens themselves have not been
hand-tested in this build: the pane header wire while an Ask waits, the
status bar notice at a narrow window, the dock's Returned card, the Settings
sidebar and the two-column launch review with long folder roots are the
things to look at. The hand tests from v0.1.69 (Settings forms and the
backup round trip) are still waiting.

Agy's loading of Parley's instructions from its added folder is still
unverified, fresh or resumed.

This is an ad-hoc-signed, unnotarized test beta. It does not update the
stable Sparkle feed or Homebrew cask. Follow the included installation
instructions.
